verse.verse_1: Nun. By the pen and what the scribes write.
verse.verse_2: By your Lord's Grace, you are not afflicted with madness,
verse.verse_3: and surely yours shall be a never-ending reward,
verse.verse_4: and you are certainly on the most exalted standard of moral excellence.
verse.verse_5: So you will soon see, and they too will see,
verse.verse_6: which of you is afflicted with madness.
verse.verse_7: Surely your Lord knows well those who have strayed from His Way just as He knows well those who are on the Right Way.
verse.verse_8: Do not, then, yield to those who reject the Truth, decrying it as false;
verse.verse_9: they would wish you to be pliant so that they too may be pliant.
verse.verse_10: And do not yield to any contemptible swearer,
verse.verse_11: the fault-finder who goes around slandering,
verse.verse_12: the hinderer of good, the transgressor, the sinful;
verse.verse_13: the coarse-grained, and above all mean and ignoble;
verse.verse_14: (who so acts) simply because he has wealth and sons,
verse.verse_15: and whenever Our verses are rehearsed to him, he says: “These are fairy- tales of times gone by.”
verse.verse_16: Soon shall We brand him on his snout.
verse.verse_17: We have put them [i.e., the Makkans] to test even as We put to test the owners of the orchard when they vowed that they would gather the fruit of their orchard in the morning,
verse.verse_18: without making any allowance (for the will of Allah).
verse.verse_19: Thereupon a calamity from your Lord passed over it while they were asleep,
verse.verse_20: and so by morning the orchard lay as though it had been fully harvested.
verse.verse_21: At daybreak they called out to one another:
verse.verse_22: “Hurry to your orchard if you would gather its fruit.”
verse.verse_23: So off they went, whispering to one another:
verse.verse_24: “No destitute person shall enter it today.”
verse.verse_25: They went forth early, believing that they had the power (to gather the fruit).
verse.verse_26: But as soon as they beheld the orchard, (they cried out): “We have certainly lost the way;
verse.verse_28: The best among them said: “Did I not say to you: why do you not give glory to (your Lord)?”
verse.verse_29: They cried out: “Glory be to our Lord! Certainly we were sinners.”
verse.verse_30: Then they began to reproach one another.
verse.verse_31: They said: “Woe to us! We had indeed transgressed.
verse.verse_32: Maybe our Lord will give us a better orchard in its place; to our Lord do we penitently turn.”
verse.verse_33: Such is the chastisement; and the chastisement of the Hereafter is assuredly even greater, if only they knew.
verse.verse_34: Surely the God-fearing shall have Gardens of bliss with their Lord.
verse.verse_35: What! Shall We treat those who have submitted (to Our command) like those who have acted as criminals?
verse.verse_36: What is the matter with you? How ill do you judge!
verse.verse_37: Or do you have a Book wherein you read
verse.verse_38: that (in the Hereafter) you shall have all that you choose for yourselves?
verse.verse_39: Or have We sworn a covenant with you which We are bound to keep till the Day of Resurrection, (a covenant requiring that whatever you ordain for yourselves shall be yours)?
verse.verse_40: Ask them: “Which of them can guarantee that?
verse.verse_41: Or has something been guaranteed by any of those whom they associate with Allah in His Divinity?” If so, let them bring forth their associates, if they are truthful.
verse.verse_42: On the Day when the dreadful calamity will unfold, when people will be summoned to prostrate themselves, and yet they will not be able to prostrate.
verse.verse_43: Their eyes shall be downcast and ignominy shall overwhelm them. For when they were safe and sound, they were summoned to prostrate themselves, (and they refused).
verse.verse_44: So leave Me, (O Prophet), to deal with him who gives the lie to this Discourse. We shall draw them little by little (to their undoing) in a way that they will not know.
verse.verse_45: I am giving them a respite. Great is My scheme!
verse.verse_46: Or are you asking them for some compensation so that they feel burdened with debt?
verse.verse_47: Or do they have any knowledge of the Unseen which they are now writing down?
verse.verse_48: So bear with patience until the Judgement of your Lord comes, and do not belike the man in the fish (i.e., Jonah) who called out, choking with grief:
verse.verse_49: had his Lord not bestowed His favour upon him, he would have been cast upon that barren shore (and would have remained there) in disgrace.
verse.verse_50: But his Lord exalted him, and included him among His righteous servants.
verse.verse_51: When the unbelievers hear this Exhortation, they look at you as though they would knock you off your feet with their (hostile) glances. They say: “Surely he is afflicted with madness”;
verse.verse_52: although this is nothing but an Exhortation (to goodness) for everyone in the world.
